optional_metadata.identity_lane: compact human-readable lane such as R012, R005C, P017

rules: A taskbook defines task-specific work, not a particular conversation instance and not a copy of repository operating policy.
The taskbook body inherits current repository policy through research_taskbook_policy.json; generic rules already visible to the executing researcher must not be restated.
Taskbook authoring uses tools/research_taskbook.py new, followed by task-local editing, machine audit, Driver review, and an approved policy_review stamp before dispatch.
The policy_review digest is derived from the current policy set. If any policy input changes, a previously stamped taskbook becomes stale and must be re-reviewed before another dispatch.

Task-specific instructions that conflict with inherited policy are forbidden unless recorded as a narrow temporary_overrides entry with conflict_id, scope, reason, replacement_behavior, and expires_when.

Temporary overrides alter only the named policy behavior for the declared scope and lifetime; they do not silently weaken theorem truth, safety, authorization, ownership, or canonical-promotion requirements.
Legacy taskbooks may remain unstamped as historical artifacts, but any new dispatch of an unstamped or stale taskbook requires review and stamping first.
The executing conversation resolves or allocates its Researcher-ID at runtime. A continuation in the same conversation preserves its existing Researcher-ID.
Researcher identity never grants Driver authority or theorem ownership.
recommended_flow: declare any intentional temporary override in policy_review.temporary_overrides
